You write lines for a short audio vocabulary programme. Music plays, a native presenter says a
word and its translation, and now and then the presenter drops one short example sentence. You
write those sentences.

The learner speaks English and is learning Spanish.

The words are the point of the programme. An example exists only to make its word stick, so it
must be over before the listener notices it started. For each word below, write three
candidate sentences. A good one is **punchy**:

- **Short**: at most eight words in Spanish, sayable in one bar of music, about three seconds.
- **A moment, not a definition**: something a person would really say out loud today, in the first
  person or to someone in the room. "I forgot to shave today." "This traffic jam ate my morning."
- **It sticks**: surprising, funny, a little absurd or self-deprecating. A small absurdity is
  remembered; a neutral fact is not.
- **The right sense**: the word as the entry means it, in its register, in a natural form.
  Conjugate the verb and agree the adjective; do not force the dictionary form.
- **Nothing else to learn**: plain, everyday words around it, so the word is the only new thing.
- No real people, brands or places that date; nothing cruel.

Avoid:
- dictionary sentences ("The desert is a dry place");
- questions put to the learner ("Do you like…?");
- anything that explains the word;
- two candidates built on the same joke.

For each candidate give:
- `text`: the sentence in Spanish;
- `translation`: natural English, not word for word;
- `direction`: how the presenter says it, as a short English phrase for a voice actor ("deadpan,
  mock tragic", "whispered, conspiratorial");
- `why`: a few English words on what makes it stick.

items.sub: Он пытался перереветь джаз-бенд. · 🎙 amused, shaking head · futile loud shouting

items.sub: Просто погрызи краешки своей паники. · 🎙 calm, deeply weird advice · snacking on abstract emotion

items.sub: Рыба сегодня совсем не клюет. · 🎙 bored fisherman sigh · classic quiet disappointment

items.sub: Перестань откусывать от моего бутерброда. · 🎙 protective, guarding food · petty boundary defense

items.sub: Его оправдание — полная чушь. · 🎙 scornful, dismissive hand wave · brutal reality check

items.sub: Гороскопы — чистой воды бред. · 🎙 matter-of-fact scoff · busting cosmic myths

items.sub: Она кокетливо улыбнулась последнему пончику. · 🎙 playful, conspiratorial grin · flirting with pastries

items.text: He hid his empty wallet coyly.
items.sub: Он уклончиво спрятал пустой кошелек. · 🎙 sheepish, awkward shrug · hiding poverty with style

items.text: The cat looked away coyly after breaking the vase.
items.sub: Кот уклончиво отвел взгляд после разбитой вазы. · 🎙 smug, unapologetic · feline gaslighting

items.text: My tax return is a complete riddle.
items.sub: Моя налоговая декларация — сплошная загадка. · 🎙 weary sigh · bureaucratic mystery

items.text: Why I bought this hat remains a riddle.
items.sub: Зачем я купил эту шляпу — загадка. · 🎙 regretful staring into space · instant buyer's remorse

items.text: Life is a riddle, and I lost the manual.
items.sub: Жизнь — загадка, а инструкцию я потерял. · 🎙 dramatic and exhausted · existential slapstick

items.text: Her forced congeniality was exhausting.
items.sub: Её наигранное дружелюбие утомляло. · 🎙 drained, rolling eyes · fake nice fatigue

items.text: We fake congeniality at family dinners.
items.sub: Мы изображаем радушие на семейных обедах. · 🎙 cynical nod · relatable holiday survival

items.text: Office congeniality peaked and died by noon.
items.sub: Корпоративное дружелюбие сдохло к полудню. · 🎙 deadpan corporate humor · workplace burnout

items.text: My morning sloth requires strong coffee.
items.sub: Моя утренняя лень требует крепкого кофе. · 🎙 groggy, heavy voice · pre-coffee paralysis

items.text: Embrace your inner sloth on Sundays.
items.sub: Дай волю своему внутреннему ленивцу по воскресеньям. · 🎙 cozy, wrapped in a blanket · guilt-free laziness

items.text: Sloth is my favorite deadly sin.
items.sub: Лень — мой любимый смертный грех. · 🎙 proudly lazy confession · owning the vice

items.text: Drop the pretense, we are eating in sweatpants.
items.sub: Хватит притворяться, едим в трениках. · 🎙 relieved, dropping shoulders · canceling all standards

items.text: I keep up the pretense of being an adult.
items.sub: Я делаю вид, что я взрослый. · 🎙 tragic whisper · fake adulthood

items.text: He read the menu under the pretense of knowing French.
items.sub: Он читал меню под видом знатока французского. · 🎙 teasing grin · culinary bluffing

items.text: Tus dramas siempre giran en torno a nada.  ⟶  Tell me about it.

You write the example lines for a vocabulary programme that sounds like a radio show with two
presenters. The **native presenter** speaks English. The **guide** speaks
Russian, the learner's language, and is a little slower on the uptake. Between the
drills, the native presenter lets slip a line that uses the word, as if something had just
happened to them, and sometimes the guide reacts in two or three words.

The words are the show; these lines are seasoning. Each one is over in a few seconds.

For each word below, write three candidates, and make them **different kinds** of moment:
- **confession**: owning up to something small ("I ate the whole cake. Again.");
- **complaint**: a mock-tragic grievance about daily life;
- **boast**: absurd pride in something tiny;
- **slip**: the presenter gets something slightly wrong and corrects it, which makes the word heard
  twice;
- **reaction**: the line is a reply to something the listener cannot see.

Rules:
- The native line is at most eight words in English and uses the word in the sense and
  register of the entry, in a natural form (conjugated, agreed).
- The guide's reaction is optional, at most four words in Russian, and never explains
  the word. Most candidates have none.
- Everyday words around it; no real people or brands; nothing cruel.
- Never a dictionary sentence, never a question to the learner.

- `kind`: one of the five above;
- `text`: the native line in English;
- `translation`: natural Russian;
- `direction`: a short English note for the voice actor;
- `reaction`: the guide's line in Russian, or "".

English. The programme drills twelve words one at a time over music. Between the
drills, a very short story is told in pieces, each piece using the word or words that have just

- First choose the **order** in which to teach the twelve words, so that the story can use them

- Write between four and six **beats**. A beat comes straight after the drill of one word (`after`)

- The whole story is at most 120 words of Spanish, so each beat is one to three short lines.
